# Test fixtures

## `tone_*.mp3`

⚠ **These are the only committed binary fixtures, and the reason is the bug they guard.**
Every other audio case in `tests/Vernacula.Tests/AudioFormatIngestionTests.cs` synthesises its
fixture with `ffmpeg` at test time and skips when `ffmpeg` is absent. MP3 cannot: the whole
point of `Mp3Decoder` is that MP3 decodes **without** `ffmpeg` installed, which is exactly the
machine where a generated fixture could not be built and the test would skip — leaving #176
(MP3 stopped working on Windows the moment #156 routed it to the `ffmpeg` executable) free to
come back unnoticed. A committed file is what makes the test run everywhere.

A 0.5 s 440 Hz tone, encoded with LAME. Regenerate with:

```sh
ffmpeg -v error -y -f lavfi -i sine=frequency=440:sample_rate=44100:duration=0.5 \
       -af volume=6 -acodec libmp3lame -b:a 32k -ac 1 tone_mono_44100.mp3

ffmpeg -v error -y -f lavfi -i sine=frequency=440:sample_rate=48000:duration=0.5 \
       -af volume=6 -acodec libmp3lame -b:a 64k -ac 2 tone_stereo_48000.mp3

ffmpeg -v error -y -f lavfi -i sine=frequency=440:sample_rate=16000:duration=0.5 \
       -af volume=6 -acodec libmp3lame -b:a 32k -ac 1 tone_mono_16000.mp3

ffmpeg -v error -y -f lavfi -i sine=frequency=440:sample_rate=8000:duration=0.5 \
       -af volume=6 -acodec libmp3lame -b:a 32k -ac 1 tone_mono_8000.mp3
```

`volume=6` lifts lavfi's -18 dBFS sine to roughly 0.75 peak, for the same reason it is applied
in `AudioFormatIngestionTests`: it keeps "is this silent?" a meaningful assertion rather than
one tuned down to meet the source.

⚠ **The four sample rates are three different MPEG variants, and that is the point.** 44.1 and
48 kHz are MPEG-1; 16 kHz is MPEG-2 (LSF, 576 samples per frame instead of 1152); 8 kHz is
MPEG-2.5. They are decoded by different paths, and the difference is not academic: NLayer
1.16.0 decodes only about half of any file at or below 24 kHz while still reporting the full
duration. A test suite carrying only 44.1/48 kHz fixtures passes against a decoder that would
silently drop half of every 16 kHz voice memo handed to it. Channel count and bitrate vary
across the four for the same reason — so the decoder's reported layout is checked against
something other than a single default.

They are small on purpose (2.4–4.5 KB each) — low bitrate and half a second, which is all a
format-routing test needs.
